To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antioxidant pretreatment of embryonic VM cell suspensions with the combination of the thiol antioxidants NAC and GSh, and the 21-aminosteroi U-83836, did not significantly improve the survival of DA neurons in vitro or in vivo.

pretreating cell suspension cultures of embryonic rat VM tissue with a member of the 21-aminsteroid family of antioxidants (U-83836E) prior to grafting into the unilateral 3-nitropropionic acid (3-NP) model of Parkinson's Disease significantly improved the survival of transplanted dopaminergic neurons and the functional recovery observed in this animal model.
pretreating VM tissue with antioxidant combinations, including U-83836, significantly improves DA neuron survival both in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the survival of DA neurons in vitro and in vivo by using antioxidant combinations to protect against oxidative stress.
developing strategies to improve the efficacy of fetal nigral transplantation for Parkinson's disease by improving the survival of grafted cells.
the use of antioxidants to protect DA neurons in the context of transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antioxidant pretreatment of embryonic VM tissue with U-8386E alone, but not in combination with NAC and GHS, significantly improves both functional recovery and survival of DA neurons in a 6-OH-DA lesioned rat model of Parkinson’s disease.

antioxidant pretreatment of cell suspensions of VM tissue can improve DA neuron survival in culture and that this can be translated into a functional benefit when grafted into the 6-OH-DA-lesioned rat model, but that the effect of pretreatment on survival is not additive and may in fact be detrimental to the survival of DA neurons.

antioxidant pretreatment of VM cell suspension prior to grafting in the 6-OH DA-lesioned rat model is beneficial in terms of DA neuron survival, but the functional recovery is less clear and may be dependent on the antioxidant used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of NAC and U-8386E is a potent in vitro antioxidant that can be applied in vivo to improve functional recovery following transplantation of embryonic VM tissue.
pretreatment with U83836E alone is the most effective antioxidant combination to improve DA neuron survival in the 6-OHDAO model of PD and that this is associated with improved functional recovery.
pretreatment with U83836E alone or in combination with NAC and GHS can improve DA neuron survival in both in vitro and in vivo models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antioxidant U-83836 E is a potent neuroprotectant of embryonic DA neurons in vitro and in vivo.
antioxidant pretreatment can improve DA neuron survival in vivo and that this effect is dependent on the antioxidant combination used.
the combination of NAC and U-838 36E is a promising antioxidant pretreatment for enhancing the survival of embryonic DA neurons in vitro and following grafting in vivo.
